SHAB · TRAVEL & HOSPITALITY

A simpler way to book a stay.

A booking flow should help people plan their stay. We used behavioral data to find where it was getting in the way—and made a few deliberate changes.

My roleProduct Designer
CollaborationProduct, data & engineering
Case study publishedSeptember 2024
The problemResearchDecisionsOutcomeReflection

The problem

Shab connects travelers with vacation rentals across Iran. On property detail pages, guests moved through separate date and guest-selection modals before booking.

Reviewing session recordings and funnel data revealed an unexpected interruption: pressing the browser’s Back button could leave the property page instead of closing the open modal. Other steps repeated information or put too much emphasis on dates guests rarely booked.

What the evidence showed

We combined Clarity session recordings, Google Analytics, Heap, and support from data analysts to understand the journey.

  • Guests sometimes left the booking flow when they only meant to go back one step.
  • 92% of completed reservations used dates within the next 14 days.
  • Repeating cancellation policies inside the guest-selection step added information already available elsewhere.

These findings suggested a focused change to the flow rather than a wholesale redesign.

The decisions

Keep navigation in context

Make Back close the modal, so guests remain on the property they are considering.

Bring related choices together

Combine dates and guest count into one interface, reducing interruptions between two closely related decisions.

Use a more relevant default

Show the next 14 days first, while keeping the full calendar available for people planning further ahead. The default could reflect common behavior without removing flexibility.

We evaluated ideas against impact and effort, discussed them with stakeholders, and tested the proposed changes internally.

What changed

~6%

Higher booking conversion after the changes.

A before-and-after comparison during a week without peak days or holidays showed improved conversion. Guest-initiated cancellations did not change significantly after the repeated cancellation-policy content was removed.

Measurement: before and after release, during a non-peak week.

What I took forward

Small interaction details deserve the same care as large features. A familiar calendar pattern or Back behavior is only useful when it fits the context of the task.

This work reinforced the value of combining qualitative behavior with funnel data—and checking that simplification preserves the choices people still need.

Thanks to Ali Faramarzi for product guidance and collaboration.
